transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-09
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Elena Morales (Redwood SE), Jade Nguyen (Redwood SE), Markus Lee (SpectraCloud VP Eng), Priya Nair (SRE Lead), Dana Ortiz (FinOps), Tom Brooks (Data Engineer)
Links shared: Deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/spectracloud-path-econ  |  Security packet: https://redwood.ai/security/spectra-pkg

00:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll kick off in about a minute, appreciate you squeezing this in today
00:24 Speaker 2 (Markus): no problem Samir, excited to see how you map costs down to our ingestion paths — we've been trying to do that in spreadsheets forever
01:02 Speaker 1 (Samir): quick agenda: demo of Console per-path dashboards, cost attribution, how batching/K-V cache and quantization levers affect unit economics, then VPC/private options and pilot next steps
02:10 Speaker 3 (Elena): jumping right into the Console, so on the left we have Routes but we call them Paths here for SpectraCloud, you can see top consumers, latency percentiles, and cost per 1k tokens
03:08 Speaker 4 (Priya): small nit — is that cost number including both model compute and egress?
03:22 Speaker 3 (Elena): yes it folds in compute and per-token model cost; egress is shown separately in the billing tab — you can toggle what you want in the view
04:15 Speaker 1 (Samir): one thing to highlight, the path-level caching shows up as a separate column, that's our automatic prefix/K-V cache, sometimes transcribed in older notes as K-V catch or K-V cash, but it's literally a KV cache in the runtime
05:46 Speaker 5 (Dana): can you show an example where batching saves money but increases p95 latency? that's what our FinOps team worries about
06:10 Speaker 3 (Elena): sure — switching to the economics mode, you can simulate a larger batch size and you get a delta view: cost per token drops by ~22% but p95 increases from 280ms to 420ms in our simulated workload
07:02 Speaker 2 (Markus): is that in Dedicated or Hosted? we need deterministic behavior for our real-time feature generation service
07:30 Speaker 1 (Samir): good question — those sim numbers are for Hosted with default routing; if you go Dedicated (reserved pools) you get tighter variance, but cost moves up a bit; Console has a toggle to compare hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment economics
08:41 Speaker 4 (Priya): and for private VPC what changes? we have strict egress rules and need KMS integration
09:06 Speaker 3 (Elena): for VPC/private we provide a private control plane and you can bring your KMS/HSM; there is a small delta in latency because of network hops but you get full audit logs and SOC2 artefacts — I mean SOC 2 artefacts
10:12 Speaker 6 (Tom): any gotchas on network egress costs when we pin models to a region? we have customers in EU and APAC
10:30 Speaker 1 (Samir): you can route by policy per-path, so EU traffic stays in EU regions; we show regional cost breakout in the per-path drilldown so you can see that egress hit per customer
11:50 Speaker 3 (Elena): here's a trick — use the path tag filters to group prompt families, that lets you split cost attribution by product feature rather than raw endpoint
12:40 Speaker 2 (Markus): nice, that would let us bill internal tribes appropriately, FinOps can see per-feature unit economics
13:15 Speaker 5 (Dana): what's the retention window on the telemetry? we need at least 12 months of per-route granularity for audits
13:42 Speaker 3 (Elena): Console standard retention is 90 days, add-on packages for 12+ months available — we'll include in the pilot SOW options
14:55 Speaker 1 (Samir): quick live demo: I'm going to open the path called "nlp-ingest/feature-extract" and show top tokens, latency histogram and per-customer cost roll-up
16:08 Speaker 2 (Markus): small interjection — sometimes our internal name is nlp-ingest-prod-1; can we alias paths?
16:20 Speaker 3 (Elena): yes aliases and tags are supported, we can map multiple endpoints to one canonical path for cost aggregation
17:35 Speaker 3 (Elena): note that the Optimize tab will surface recommended quantization profiles for each model based on your traffic mix — in this case it recommends int8-qat for batch heavy flows
18:50 Speaker 6 (Tom): how reliable are the model quality regressions when you quantize? we can't accept a noticeable drop in accuracy
19:12 Speaker 3 (Elena): we run evals against your held out prompts — quality monitoring is built in, and Console will flag regressions and can auto-roll back to a higher precision model if metrics dip
20:44 Speaker 5 (Dana): security: SSO + SAML + RBAC, can we lock views so only FinOps sees dollar columns?
21:05 Speaker 1 (Samir): yes RBAC is roleable, you can hide columns via role policies; audit logs tie actions to user ids and are exportable
22:30 Speaker 4 (Priya): curious about throughput — if we push bursts to 10k rps do you autoscale and how does that change per-token cost?
23:00 Speaker 3 (Elena): autoscaling is configurable; for burst policies Console sim shows cost delta and expected latency envelope; also worth considering Dedicated pools for predictable tail latencies
24:12 Speaker 2 (Markus): benchmark request — can you run a baseline with our traffic and 95th percentile target of 350ms?
24:30 Speaker 1 (Samir): yes we can, Elena will run that as part of the pilot benchmark — we'll need your traffic profile and sample prompts
25:50 Speaker 6 (Tom): will the benchmark include the KV cache warm-up? that's important for cold-starts
26:05 Speaker 3 (Elena): yes we'll do warm-up runs, cold and warm curves — sometimes older notes say the runtime uses "continuous batching" and that's what we emulate
27:40 Speaker 5 (Dana): on billing, do you export GL-level line items we can plug into our accounting system?
28:00 Speaker 1 (Samir): yes per-path line items and tags export to CSV/BigQuery; we can also push into most billing systems via webhooks
29:22 Speaker 2 (Markus): any questions on compliance? the security packet link you shared earlier looks promising, will review with legal
29:45 Speaker 3 (Elena): quick note: private deployments have an extra compliance review step and a checklist for air-gapped installs if needed
31:05 Speaker 3 (Elena): demo note — when you hover over the per-token cost it shows the breakdown (model, infra, caching benefit), sometimes the transcription reads that as model infra and k-v cash which caused confusion earlier
32:40 Speaker 6 (Tom): what's a typical delta in unit cost between int8 quantized hosted and full fp16 dedicated?
33:10 Speaker 3 (Elena): ballpark: hosted+int8 ~0.6x of fp16 hosted; Dedicated fp16 maybe 0.9x of hosted fp16 depending on utilization — lot of nuance, which is why Console has the compare view
34:28 Speaker 5 (Dana): customers also ask about vendor lock — if we want to move models later how hard is migration?
34:50 Speaker 1 (Samir): we support exporting model artifacts and provide documented rollback and migration paths; plus the API surface remains consistent so your devs don't rewrite code when switching backends
36:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): latency SLOs — do you offer SLA credits if you miss the SLO in Dedicated?
36:21 Speaker 1 (Samir): Dedicated contracts include SLA targets and credits; Hosted has best-effort but we publish latency profiles per model in the catalog
37:48 Speaker 3 (Elena): for the pilot we suggest 4 weeks: week 1 ingest and mapping, week 2 perf run + config, week 3 tuning (batching, cache), week 4 review + SOW for next stage
39:12 Speaker 2 (Markus): sounds good. what's the estimated cost for a 4-week pilot with 2 reserved GPUs in Dedicated?
39:35 Speaker 1 (Samir): I'll include two price scenarios in the follow-up: Hosted pilot and Dedicated pilot; estimate and exact numbers in the deck and SOW
41:00 Speaker 6 (Tom): any blockers to start from our side? we need to share traffic and also whitelist Redwood IPs for VPC peering
41:18 Speaker 1 (Samir): yes we'll include the IP ranges and onboarding checklist in the SOW
42:33 Speaker 3 (Elena): quick demo wrap, also showing anomaly detection — Console flags unusual per-path cost spikes and links you to examples of requests that caused it
43:45 Speaker 5 (Dana): how actionable are those anomalies? can we auto-scale or auto-fallback if a model suddenly spikes in latency?
44:00 Speaker 3 (Elena): you can set auto-fallback policies to a cheaper model variant or route to a lower-latency regional pool automatically
45:20 Speaker 2 (Markus): competitor question, we've seen similar features in other platforms but not with as tight cost simulation — what's Redwood's edge?
45:42 Speaker 1 (Samir): two things: the unified model-to-runtime telemetry that ties prompts to cost, and the Optimize suggestions that are prescriptive (quant profiles, batching, cache) tied to real metrics; plus the same APIs across hosted/dedicated/private
47:05 Speaker 6 (Tom): okay last quick thing — do you support per-customer billing tags so we can invoice our end customers?
47:22 Speaker 3 (Elena): yes tags are first class, you can export cost by tag and integrate into billing or internal chargeback systems
48:55 Speaker 1 (Samir): recap and next steps: we'll send pricing deck + SOW, Elena will run perf benchmark once we get sample traffic, Markus will share prompts and whitelist IPs; follow-up scheduled 2027-06-18 14:00 UTC
50:02 Speaker 2 (Markus): thanks everyone, appreciate the thorough demo
50:10 Speaker 5 (Dana): thanks, looking forward to the pilot details
50:20 Speaker 6 (Tom): we'll aim to get you the traffic by Friday
50:35 Speaker 3 (Elena): thanks, we'll put the action items in the SOW and slack thread
51:00 Meeting end

Notes on transcription quality: medium — multiple speaker labels inferred, occasional mis-heard terms (K-V cash, continuous batching as cont batching), proper nouns occasionally off.
